reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows precipitation strengthening in an aged complex concentrated alloy at 750 °C, but it refers to room-temperature yield strength, not elevated-temperature performance. E2 only notes carbide size differences at boundaries, offering no support for nanoscale coherent precipitates, dislocation hindrance, or high-temperature strengthening. Thus, the key premises linking the intervention to improved high-temperature yield strength lack direct prior evidence.
premises: Carbon addition plus aging can form nanoscale coherent carbide precipitates in refractory HEAs
These precipitates hinder dislocation motion (precipitation strengthening)
Precipitation strengthening improves yield strength at elevated temperatures (≥850 K)
The strengthening mechanism is effective in BCC refractory HEAs under extreme environments
